title: Speed over judgement is winning the AI arms race
gist: The Pentagon's 'AI First' strategy under Pete Hegseth prioritises speed in integrating AI and autonomy into the US military, as AI-enabled targeting and autonomous drones spread across Ukraine, the Gulf, Israel, China and South Korea. The author warns that an arms race for first-mover advantage will neglect safety, and that autonomous weapons complicate deterrence because credibly signalling their deployment is hard and machines lack human judgement.

insights.claim: US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, launching the Pentagon's 'AI First' strategy at SpaceX's Starbase, framed rapid AI and autonomy integration around Elon Musk's algorithm of questioning requirements, deleting the dumb ones and accelerating.
insights.speaker: Ved Shinde
insights.so_what: The US defence establishment is explicitly prioritising speed of AI adoption, favouring fast-moving defence-tech suppliers.
insights.quote: Winning requires a new playbook. Elon wrote it with his algorithm: question every requirement, delete the dumb ones, and accelerate like hell.

insights.claim: Michael Horowitz's counterfactual of autonomous weapons enforcing the Cuban missile crisis blockade suggests automatic firing could, in theory, strengthen deterrence by shifting the onus of conflict onto the adversary.
insights.speaker: Ved Shinde
insights.so_what: Autonomy could be used as a commitment device in crises.

insights.claim: Autonomous deterrence breaks down because it is hard to persuasively communicate that autonomous weapons are actually deployed — the adversary may assume a bluff — and technical failure could cause accidental firing with unclear accountability.

insights.claim: Humans may be less efficient than agentic machines, but their ability to see an opponent's perspective and step back from the precipice is what deterrence depends on and what machines lack.
insights.speaker: Ved Shinde
insights.so_what: Argues for retaining human judgement in escalation decisions even as speed-driven doctrines dominate.
insights.quote: That ability to step back from the precipice and fathom the consequences of our own actions is the heart missing from the machine.
